topics.label: Course introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional modalities of cancer treatment—surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their associated systemic toxicities and efflux-mediated drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer-specific vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic defects in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair pathways through synthetic lethality.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic driver kinases and overcoming inhibitor resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on kinase oncogene addiction, structural mechanisms of small-molecule kinase inhibitors, and clinical challenges involving off-target effects, bypass pathways, and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the design and therapeutic mechanisms of targeted monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates directed against tumor surface antigens.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence for natural immune surveillance and evaluate strategies to harness T-cell responses against cancer, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, BiTEs, and CAR-T cell therapies.

topics.label: Broader challenges, historical trends, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics provide an overarching evaluation of cancer management, discussing treatment heterogeneity, historical mortality trends, emerging paradigms, and ethical dilemmas in clinical trial design.
